title: Protocol and Terminal
premise: Xanthe Winterbourne, a clone created to inherit the identity and unfinished business of her murdered original, arrives at Meridian Deep, a decommissioned mining colony officially listed as evacuated. She finds two hundred people the bureaucracy erased, a reactor counting down toward an unexplained shutdown, and children who share a recurring dream of fire and screaming that matches no surviving record. As she investigates her original's death, she uncovers evidence of a massacre committed by the corporation that founded the colony—a massacre scrubbed from every archive, including the one inside her own cloned memories. Xanthe must choose between the loyalty she owes her dead original's allies and the truth that will destroy them all, broadcasting proof of the massacre in the final minutes before the reactor dies, then choosing to stay with the colony rather than escape with her inheritance intact.
about_author: Ivo Nakamura is a former systems auditor who spent six years documenting abandoned industrial sites across three continents before turning to fiction. Protocol and Terminal is their fourth novel and the first written after a residency aboard a decommissioned orbital research station.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Xanthe Winterbourne arrives at Meridian Deep on a supply skiff, carrying her original's legal identity and a sealed murder file. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: cold disorientation—she is walking into a life she remembers but never lived.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Ghosts
chapters.summary: Xanthe finds the colony occupied despite official records declaring it evacuated. The residents regard her with wary recognition; some knew the original. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: uncanny unease as she realizes the paperwork is the lie.

chapters.title: Terminal Nine
chapters.summary: Colony engineer Dov Rask shows Xanthe the reactor: a countdown timer running toward an automatic shutdown with no override. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: creeping dread—the colony has weeks, not years.

chapters.title: The Murder File
chapters.summary: Alone, Xanthe opens her original's case file: fragmented notes about 'the audit,' names redacted, a final entry cut mid-sentence. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: grief for a woman she was copied from.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Teacher Mara Osei reports that eleven children describe an identical dream: fire, a sealed door, screaming in unison. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: maternal fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: A corporate liaison, Edric Voss, arrives unannounced, offering evacuation contracts that require signing away all claims against Halcyon Extraction. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: recognition of a predator wearing courtesy.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Xanthe interviews the original's old ally, Sef Ibarra, who tests her loyalty before hinting at a buried incident called the Culling. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: bitter distrust thawing into cautious alliance.

chapters.title: Dream Logic
chapters.summary: Mara records the children's dream in detail; the geography matches a level of the colony that appears on no current schematic. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Level Negative Four
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Dov find a bricked-over access shaft behind the water reclamation plant. Behind it: scorched walls. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: physical confirmation that something terrible happened here.

chapters.title: The Empty Archive
chapters.summary: Xanthe requests the colony's corporate records via relay; the response returns sanitized, dates missing, personnel files void. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: fury at the elegance of the erasure.

chapters.title: Loyalty of the Living
chapters.summary: Sef warns Xanthe that pursuing the truth will get the colonists' evacuation contracts revoked. He asks whose side she's on. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: the first open fracture between truth and survival.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe picks Voss's quarters and finds his real orders: assess liability, recommend termination of assets. The colony is a line item. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: cold clarity—she is racing a deliberate execution.

chapters.title: The Dreamer Who Woke Up
chapters.summary: One child, Tally, stops dreaming and starts drawing instead: a door, a number, a name. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: hope that memory can be recovered deliberately.

chapters.title: Bone and Slag
chapters.summary: Dov's structural survey of Level -4 reveals human remains fused into the slagged floor—far more than an accident explains. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: a stoic man quietly breaking.

chapters.title: Countdown Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Xanthe recalculates the reactor timeline and realizes the shutdown date coincides exactly with the Culling's anniversary. Someone scheduled this. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past is repeating on purpose.

chapters.title: The Clone Question
chapters.summary: Colonists confront Xanthe: is she the original returned, or a company product sent to finish the job? POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: loneliness of being neither the dead nor the living.

chapters.title: Ibarra's Confession
chapters.summary: Sef admits he survived the Culling by hiding, and that the original Winterbourne died trying to broadcast proof. He gives her her first physical clue: a data shard hidden in the mine. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Into the Mine
chapters.summary: Xanthe, Dov, and Tally's older brother Jem descend into the flooded lower galleries to retrieve the shard. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: claustrophobic determination.

chapters.title: What the Shard Holds
chapters.summary: The shard contains partial security footage: armed contractors, civilians fleeing, a sealed blast door. Timestamps match the children's dream. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by horror.

chapters.title: Voss Tightens
chapters.summary: Voss announces accelerated 'voluntary relocation' and cuts the colony's comms relay. Isolation begins. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: bureaucratic menace—he believes he is being reasonable.

chapters.title: The Children March
chapters.summary: The children, led by Tally, walk to the sealed door in their dreams' geography and refuse to leave until it's opened. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: awe at children forcing adults to face what they buried.

chapters.title: Opening the Door
chapters.summary: Dov breaches the blast door. Inside: a shelter where colonists barricaded themselves during the Culling, preserved like a tomb. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: reverent devastation.

chapters.title: Names
chapters.summary: Mara helps colonists identify the dead from personal effects. Grief becomes testimony; survivors begin recording statements. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into witness.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Day
chapters.summary: Reconstructing from the shard and Sef's account, Xanthe pieces together how her original was killed—and by whom: Voss's predecessor, now a director. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: rage with nowhere safe to put it.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone destroys the shard backup and wounds Dov. The colony suspects each other; Voss offers protection in exchange for silence. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: paranoia poisoning solidarity.

chapters.title: Jem's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jem confesses he leaked the dig site's location to Voss in exchange for his family's evacuation priority. POV: Jem. Emotional beat: shame and the desperate arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: Xanthe's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Xanthe discovers a second clone protocol in her own genetic contract: her memories were curated, the Culling excised. She was built to forget. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: violation—her mind itself was part of the cover-up.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: The colony votes: accept Voss's contracts and live, or hold the evidence and risk everything. It splits nearly down the middle. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: democracy as heartbreak.

chapters.title: Voss's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Voss gives forty-eight hours before he seals the colony and lets the reactor countdown stand, framing any deaths as equipment failure. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: self-justifying certainty cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Tally's Door
chapters.summary: Tally reveals the dream's final image she'd withheld: a second survivor, still alive when the door closed, holding a recorder. The full footage may exist. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: a thread of hope pulled taut.

chapters.title: The Recorder
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Jem search the shelter ruins and find the recorder embedded in slag, damaged but intact. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: trembling triumph.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Dov, bandaged, works through the night splicing the recorder's storage matrix. Fragments play: faces, names, the moment the door sealed. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: exhausted devotion.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Price
chapters.summary: Voss's strike team raids the colony for the recorder. Sef dies holding the corridor so the others can scatter. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the only currency he had left.

chapters.title: Scattered
chapters.summary: With the recorder split among trusted hands, the colonists hide in the deep galleries while the countdown enters its final day. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: terror braided with fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Terminal Nine
chapters.summary: Xanthe confronts Voss at the reactor control room, offering him the chance to evacuate everyone honestly. He refuses; she triggers the manual broadcast array. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the moment loyalty to the living outweighs fear.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: The full Culling footage transmits on every open channel as the reactor begins its final sequence. Off-world, the story cannot be unheard. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: release—the truth loose beyond recall.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: An evacuation skiff arrives for Xanthe alone, her inheritance restored if she leaves. She sends the skiff back empty and stays. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: renouncing the inheritance to claim the legacy.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Investigators arrive to a colony that refused to die; the reactor is stabilized by jury-rigged repairs. Voss is taken into custody, protesting procedure. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: weary, imperfect justice.

chapters.title: What the Children Dream Now
chapters.summary: The shared dream changes: the door stands open, the dead walk out into light. Tally says they're saying goodbye. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief finding its natural end.

chapters.title: Protocol and Terminal
chapters.summary: Months later, Xanthe writes the true record in her own name—not the original's, her own. The colony rebuilds; the memorial lists every name. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: quiet arrival—she was never a copy of anyone's ending.
